comments.story: Engine cooling – why rocket engines don’t melt
comments.why: Series detailing V2 parts, this one on the turbopump
comments.text: If that interests you then this series of videos is definitely worth watching. It details several parts of the German V2 missile, the grand father of all modern liquid propellant rockets. This one is about the turbopump which is one of the most interesting parts. [VIDEO]

comments.author: liability
comments.why: Long documentary on V2 turbopumps and peroxide catalysis
comments.text: The German V2 rockets also used hydrogen peroxide and a catalyst (sodium or possibly potassium permanganate) to drive their turbopumps (which pumped LOx and alcohol into the engine.) Here's a pretty good 2.5 hour long documentary about the V2 turbopumps specifically: [VIDEO] (The H2O2/catalyst system is discussed/demonstrated around the 45 minute mark.)
